text:
jamie: noticing a p99 latency surge on pool-gpu-3 since 12:05UTC. throughput dropped ~25%. KV-cache evictions spiked. looks correlated with a tenant sending lots of short-seq requests.

opsbot: incident created INC-2026-042 (performance - pool-gpu-3 p99 spike). page oncall.

sanjay: on it. can someone attach flameprof and kernel-selection logs for the window? also which model variants were active?

leila: attaching short logs from 12:03-12:09 (snipped):
```
[12:04:55] kernel_autoswitch: try switch -> llama-13b-opt /chan 2
[12:05:01] kvcache: evict tenant=acme-corp stripe=7 count=412
[12:05:02] kernel_switch: fallback -> quantized-8bit due to OOM_HINT
[12:05:03] batcher: continuous batching depth drop from 8 -> 2
[12:05:10] latency.p99 increased 220ms -> 1.8s
```

leila: flameprof gist: https://gph.redwood/leila/flame-176875 (high kernel-switch churn + batch fragmentation).

ryan: sounds like kernel_autoswitch is oscillating under mixed short/long load and causing kvcache churn. quick mitigation: temporarily disable kernel_autoswitch for pool-gpu-3 and pin to the stable kernel. also rate-limit the noisy tenant.

maya: +1. proposed immediate actions: 1) flag off autoswitch on pool-gpu-3, 2) add tenant-level soft throttle (burst 200req/min -> 80req/min), 3) route seq<=32 to quantized-8bit static kernel to avoid switching.

jamie: can we do these without a full deploy? prefer flag + routing rule changes if possible.

leila: we have FF controlplane. curl toggles work:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FLAGS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"kernel_autoswitch","pool":"pool-gpu-3","value":false}'
```

deploy-bot: rollout request received for flag kernel_autoswitch -> false (scope: pool-gpu-3). gating checks passed. proceeding.

deploy-bot: flag rollout succeeded (95% hosts) at 12:11UTC.

opsbot: update INC-2026-042: flag kernel_autoswitch disabled on pool-gpu-3; applying tenant soft throttle to tenant=acme-corp.

ryan: applying tenant throttle via routing policy, config snippet:
```
route_rule {
  tenant_id: "acme-corp"
  pool: "pool-gpu-3"
  rate_limit_rps: 1.3  # ~80/min
  burst: 10
}
```

ryan: throttle applied at 12:12UTC. routing rule pushed to edge.

leila: reran perf window 12:12-12:18: p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 310ms, throughput back to ~95% baseline, kvcache evictions reduced by 87%. flameprof shows kernel switch churn gone.

jamie: nice. any downstream regressions from pinning kernel? e.g., CPU utilization, tail latency on long-seq?

leila: small increase in avg CPU on pool hosts (+6%) but stable. long-seq p95 unchanged. monitoring panels: https://dash.redwood/pools/pool-gpu-3

opsbot: INC-2026-042 status -> mitigated. resolution candidate after postmortem.

maya: next steps (owners):
- sanjay: postmortem + timeline (due EOD)
- leila: collect full flameprof and attach (done)
- ryan: plan for adaptive batching tweak to avoid fragmentation when mixing short/long sequences (PR draft)
- jamie: check if model variants catalog needs explicit routing rules for short sequences

sanjay: starting postmortem. initial hypothesis: kernel_autoswitch heuristic is too sensitive to transient OOM_HINT signals when multi-tenant short-seq load spikes, which triggers fallback kernels and causes KV cache hotstripe churn. will propose: smoothing window for autoswitch decision + kvcache eviction hysteresis.

jamie: thanks everyone. keep updates in thread. once postmortem is up ping #eng-all. :thumbsup:

opsbot: INC-2026-042 closed as mitigated by ops on 12:20UTC.

sanjay: postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood/pm/postmortems/INC-2026-042 (will iterate).

maya: follow-up: schedule a short tech huddle tomorrow to review batching heuristics and kernel selection thresholds.

jamie: agreed. end of thread.
